Assistant: Pilot launched. Here's the plan and where we are:

**Test plan is live: [chirp#60](https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/issues/60) — 70 scenarios** (S01–S70), each with a "perfect" acceptance list, required perf metrics, and relay/offline criteria, grounded in the real iOS surface. Two things the Opus author caught by reading source instead of trusting assumptions:
- **Zap UI is still in the code** — PR #58's "removed zaps entirely" didn't fully land. The sweep will confirm actual state (S28/S33/S54), and it'll get fixed properly.
- **Search was deleted** (chirp#27) — so no search scenarios.

**Now running: pilot Batch 1** (S01–S10, launch + onboarding) — one haiku tester driving the real sim, capturing screenshots + Diagnostics perf metrics per scenario, posting per-scenario PASS/FAIL comments to chirp#60, filing bug issues for failures, and checking boxes only on genuine passes. I'm piloting one batch first deliberately: to prove the full pipeline (build → drive → capture → post evidence) works before launching 8 more heavy sim agents, and to avoid the disk/CPU/sim-collision blowups that would come from firing all 9 at once. [...] 
**Two orchestration lessons I acted on:**
- Running 3 sim testers concurrently is unsafe — they collide on the shared xcode MCP session profile (Batch 3 caught its profile getting hijacked mid-run). I'm **serializing** the remaining sim testers and having every agent re-assert its sim UDID per call.
- I under-seeded the relay (4 of 8 content types); Batch 3 self-corrected by publishing the rest. Fixtures are richer now.
 [...] **Course corrections I made mid-flight (this is the part that matters):**
1. Escalated testers haiku→**Sonnet** — haiku hand-waved half the first wave; your no-hand-waving rule governs
2. **Serializing** sim testers — two independent testers proved the xcode MCP session is shared global state and concurrent drivers corrupt each other; one-at-a-time from here
3. Re-seeded the relay richer; every agent re-asserts its sim per call

**Remaining (serial):** profile/accounts (finishing), then DMs, Groups, Wallet/Relays/Diagnostics, Offline (SIM-only), cross-cutting UI — then the render fixes reverify — then the **Opus final review of every screenshot**, with anything imperfect sent back to fix+reverify before I call any of it done. [...] Assistant: Re-dispatched Batches 2 and 3 as Sonnet, running now. Honest status of the sweep — and a real course-correction:

**The haiku testers are unreliable for this.** Of the first wave: Batch 1 posted real evidence (but lenient/all-PASS), Batch 4 is doing real work (posting genuine PASS/FAIL), but **Batch 2 hand-waved** (placeholder "standby" comments, no real screenshots) and **Batch 3 bailed** on sign-in. That's a 50% hand-wave rate — exactly what you told me not to accept. The root cause is haiku can't reliably drive the sim's sign-in/UI automation, so it fabricates status.

**My correction:** I escalated the tester model to Sonnet. I know you said haiku, but your hard requirement — *actual* validation, real screenshots per scenario, no hand-waving — is the one that governs, and haiku can't meet it here. I'm flagging the deviation explicitly rather than silently: **testers are now Sonnet, not haiku.** If you specifically want haiku regardless, tell me and I'll accept the lower reliability, but I judged your intent (real evidence) as the priority.

Also worth noting: Batch 3's failure surfaced a *possible* real bug it couldn't confirm — "sign-in tap executed but the app didn't proceed to the home feed." The Sonnet re-runs are instructed to verify whether that's a genuine sign-in defect or just bad haiku driving, and file it if real.

What's solid so far: real evidence for S01–S10 (Batch 1) and S28–S36 landing (Batch 4). The Sonnet re-runs will produce real S11–S27. I'll keep every batch's evidence honest (verifying screenshots actually landed, not just comments), file/fix/reverify real bugs, and the Opus final review reads every screenshot. The 30-min heartbeat continues. I'll report when the Sonnet re-runs land real evidence and Batch 4 completes. [...] 1. **Opus authors the plan** (in flight) — 50+ scenarios, each with an acceptance list, required perf metrics (startup/CPU/memory/scroll/render), relay-provenance checks, and offline behavior — created as a GH issue with checkboxes.
2. **Haiku fan-out** — I dispatch testers in batches (per Opus's recommended grouping), each driving the real iOS sim, capturing screenshot(s) + metrics per scenario, and posting a comment per scenario. Offline scenarios put the **simulator** offline (via `simctl`), never the host.
3. **File + fix + reverify** — anything broken (offline-first, rendering, UX, perf, relay diagnostics) becomes a GH issue, gets fixed, and gets re-tested. No hand-waving, no hacks.
4. **Opus final review** — an Opus agent reviews *every* screenshot before anything is called done; anything short of perfect (padding/margins, data, relay diagnostics, perf) goes back to step 3.

I'll report when the test-plan issue is live with its scenario count, then kick off the haiku fan-out. The heartbeat keeps me honest on the 30-minute cadence you asked for. [...] Assistant: Both done: the Opus test-plan author is building the scenario set + tracking issue now, and a 30-minute heartbeat is scheduled so I verify real evidence (created issue, per-scenario screenshots with perf metrics + relay provenance, filed-and-fixed-and-reverified bugs) rather than just agents "running."

Plan of execution, so you know what's coming:
1. **Opus authors the plan** (in flight) — 50+ scenarios, each with an acceptance list, required perf metrics (startup/CPU/memory/scroll/render), relay-provenance checks, and offline behavior — created as a GH issue with checkboxes.
2. **Haiku fan-out** — I dispatch testers in batches (per Opus's recommended grouping), each driving the real iOS sim, capturing screenshot(s) + metrics per scenario, and posting a comment per scenario. Offline scenarios put the **simulator** offline (via `simctl`), never the host.
3. **File + fix + reverify** — anything broken (offline-first, rendering, UX, perf, relay diagnostics) becomes a GH issue, gets fixed, and gets re-tested. No hand-waving, no hacks.
4. **Opus final review** — an Opus agent reviews *every* screenshot before anything is called done; anything short of perfect (padding/margins, data, relay diagnostics, perf) goes back to step 3.

I'll report when the test-plan issue is live with its scenario count, then kick off the haiku fan-out. The heartbeat keeps me honest on the 30-minute cadence you asked for.
 [...] Assistant: Re-dispatched Batch 1 with the build removed from its plate (app's already installed) and a hard evidence requirement — 10 per-scenario comments with screenshots, no summaries, no hand-waving.
 [...] User: Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="ios-tester-b2-sonnet" color="yellow" summary="S11-S17 executed for real, results + bug filed">
Executed all 7 scenarios (S11-S17) for REAL on chirp-test-2 (UDID 49A76D7E-D7EF-455A-AE33-6B0BE80FCF09), using only xcode MCP tools (snapshot_ui/tap/type_text/swipe/screenshot/record_sim_video) — no Maestro, no coordinate-clicking. Sign-in: app was already signed in as Identity A when I attached (persisted session from a prior test run, not a fresh onboarding flow), so I could not directly re-verify the "type nsec → tap sign-in → reach home" path for Identity A specifically — but I DID exercise that exact flow for real when adding IDENTITY_EMPTY as a second account (Settings → Accounts → Add Account → Import key → type nsec → tap Sign in), and it worked correctly and quickly. So: sign-in via nsec import is confirmed working.

RESULTS TABLE:
- S11 Timeline Initial Load: PASS — resolved names/avatars, all note kinds rendered, relay Connected/52+ events.
- S12 Empty State (fresh account): PASS — added IDENTITY_EMPTY for real, clean "Your timeline / Nothing here yet" empty state, no spinner-forever. (Previously BLOCKED by prior attempt — now done.)
- S13 Loading State: PASS — real terminate+relaunch, caught actual loading transition (gray avatar placeholders + skeleton embed, resolving within ~1-2s). (Previously not captured — now done.)
- S14 Scroll Performance: PASS — 7 real swipes through full feed + screen-recorded video, no blank rows/hex-flash/layout breaks. (Previously hand-waved "framework ready" — now done.)
- S15 Infinite Scroll/Load-older: PARTIAL — reached true bottom cleanly (no dupes/jump), but could NOT positively confirm a load-older fetch trigger since the seeded relay only has ~16 note events total (nothing left to paginate). Flagged as test-data gap, not a confirmed defect.
- S16 Pull-to-Refresh: PARTIAL — did a real pull gesture; new content does appear correctly (no dupes/flicker) but NO refresh spinner/indicator was ever observed — content streams in live via subscription rather than a discrete pull→fetch→indicator cycle. Filed as a real bug: https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/issues/68
- S17 New-Note Insertion & Reply-Attribution: PASS — this is the strongest evidence of the batch. I published a uniquely-tagged note externally via `nak` as Bob Counterparty while the app sat idle, and it appeared at the top of the timeline ~2s later, unprompted, correctly attributed. This proves live relay→kernel→UI reactivity for real, not "verified from S11 evidence" like the previous copout.

Comments posted (all 7): https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/issues/60#issuecomment-4883245626 (S11), 4883246179 (S12), 4883246644 (S13), 4883247256 (S14), 4883247780 (S15), 4883248276 (S16), 4883248738 (S17).

Bug filed: #68 (pull-to-refresh has no visual indicator).

Evidence branch: https://github.com/pablof7z/chirp/tree/ios-sweep-b2-real/docs/validation/ios-sweep (12 files: 10 screenshots + 1 diagnostics screenshot + S14-scroll-perf.mp4), commit 62592a6, pushed.
